Every project follows the same simple process: we inspect, explain what we found, give you a clear estimate, schedule the work, and finish with a quality-control check.

sections.body: You don't have to know the right term before you call. Start with what you're seeing, and we'll confirm the rest on site. Here's a quick guide:

No visible problem, but the roof is getting older: book a roof inspection.

Repeated leaks or a roof near the end of its life: look at roof replacement.
An office, retail or multi-family building: see commercial roofing.

sections.body: Valley homes and buildings use a handful of roof systems, and many properties have more than one. A house might have concrete tile over the living area and a spray foam section over the patio. We work on all of them:
bullets: Concrete and clay tile roofs, including underlayment replacement
Asphalt shingle roofs
Spray foam roofs and recoats
Elastomeric coatings
Flat and low-slope roofs
Sloped roofs of every common pitch

sections.h2: What Arizona does to a roof
sections.body:
Roofs here wear out differently than they do in milder climates. Summer heat and strong UV dry out sealants, bake asphalt shingles and break down the top coat on foam and flat roofs. On tile roofs, the tiles often outlast the underlayment beneath them, which commonly starts to wear out after about 20–25 years.

Monsoon season, June 15–September 30, adds sudden wind and heavy rain that find any weak spot. That's why we recommend an inspection in spring and a quick check after major storms. Small fixes made early usually cost far less than water damage inside the house.

sections.h2: Repair or replace: how we decide
sections.body:
We look at the roof's age, how widespread the problem is, and how often it has needed work. An isolated issue on a sound roof is almost always a repair. Failing underlayment across a whole tile roof, or shingles worn bare on every slope, usually points to replacement.

We'll show you photos and explain the reasoning so you can make the call. For cost questions, our roofing cost guide explains what drives the price. Every roof is different, so your estimate is based on your roof.

Call our Gilbert office at 602-548-3770, Monday to Friday, 7 am to 5 pm. If we don't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours.

Phone is the only way to reach us, which keeps things simple: you talk to a person who can schedule a visit and answer questions about your roof. Our office is closed on Saturday and Sunday.

faqs: What roofing services does Integrity Roofing offer?

Roof repair, preventive maintenance, inspections, roof replacement and re-roofing, damaged-roof and storm repair, foam roof recoating, elastomeric coatings, and commercial roofing, for homes and businesses across the Phoenix Valley.
Do you only do one type of roof?
No. We work on tile, asphalt shingle, spray foam, flat/low-slope, sloped and coated roofs, so our recommendation is based on what your building actually needs.
How do I get started?
Call the office at 602-548-3770, Monday to Friday, 7 am to 5 pm, and we'll schedule a time to look at your roof. If we don't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours.
Do you handle small repairs or only big projects?
Both. Small repairs like replacing broken tiles, fixing flashing or sealing a penetration are a big part of what we do, alongside full replacements.
Are your crews licensed?
Integrity Roofing is licensed with the Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC #096629) and is bonded and insured.
Is financing available for larger projects?
Yes, financing options are available. Ask about them during your estimate.
How much do roofing services cost?

It depends on the roof type, size, pitch, access and what the work involves. Our roofing cost guide at /resources/roofing-cost-guide/ explains the main cost factors. Every roof is different, so we give you an estimate after looking at yours.
What areas do you serve?

We work across the Phoenix Valley, including Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler, Queen Creek, San Tan Valley, Tempe, Phoenix, Scottsdale, Apache Junction, Ahwatukee, Glendale and Peoria. Our office is in Gilbert.
What's the difference between a roof repair and a re-roof?

A repair fixes a specific problem, such as a broken tile, a failed flashing or a leaking vent. A re-roof replaces the roof system across the whole roof, either with new materials or, on tile, by installing new underlayment and reinstalling the tiles.
When is the best time of year to schedule roof work?
Spring is ideal for inspections and repairs because it's before monsoon season starts on June 15. That said, a leak or damaged roof should be looked at as soon as you notice it, whatever the season.
Do you recoat foam roofs?
Yes. Spray foam roofs need a fresh protective coating on a schedule, and we handle foam repairs, recoats and elastomeric coatings for homes and commercial buildings.
What are your office hours?
Monday to Friday, 7 am to 5 pm. We're closed Saturday and Sunday. If we don't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours.

repairs-and-maintenance.title: Roof Repair & Maintenance in Gilbert, AZ | Integrity Roofing
repairs-and-maintenance.desc: Roof leak repair, broken tile replacement, flashing repair and preventive maintenance in Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler & Phoenix. Family-owned since 1993.
repairs-and-maintenance.h1: Roof repair and maintenance that adds years to your roof
repairs-and-maintenance.lead: Leaks, cracked tiles, lifted shingles, worn flashing, blistered foam: we find the cause, fix it properly, and help you keep your roof in shape so small problems don't become big ones.
repairs-and-maintenance.answer: Most roof leaks in Arizona come from cracked or slipped tiles, worn underlayment, failed flashing around vents and walls, or aging coatings on flat roofs. Integrity Roofing inspects the roof to find the real source, repairs it, and can set up routine maintenance so your roof lasts as long as possible.
repairs-and-maintenance.card_text: Leak repair, broken tiles, flashing and preventive maintenance.

sections.body: A good repair starts with finding where the water is really getting in, which is often not directly above the stain on your ceiling. We trace the problem, show you what we found, and repair it with materials that match your roof.
bullets: Leak detection and repair
Cracked, broken or slipped tile replacement
Shingle replacement after wind damage
Flashing repair at walls, chimneys, skylights and vents
Valley and ridge repairs
Foam roof blister and puncture repair
Flat roof seam and drain repairs
Roof penetration sealing (solar, satellite, plumbing vents)

sections.body:
You change your car's oil so the engine lasts. Roofs are the same. Regular maintenance, such as clearing debris, replacing a few broken tiles, resealing flashings and recoating foam on schedule, is far less expensive than the water damage it prevents.

In Arizona, intense UV and heat break down sealants and coatings faster than in milder climates, so routine checks matter even more here.
bullets: Debris removal from valleys, gutters and roof drains
Replacing broken or displaced tiles and shingles
Resealing flashing and roof penetrations
Checking and recoating foam and flat roofs
Photo report of roof condition

sections.h2: How we track down a leak
sections.body:
Water travels. It can enter at a cracked tile near the ridge, run down the underlayment or along a rafter, and show up as a stain several feet away. Patching the spot above the stain often misses the real cause.

We start with what you've noticed: where the stain is, when it appears, and whether it only leaks in wind-driven rain. Then we check the roof above and uphill of that spot, including flashing, penetrations, valleys and the condition of the tiles, shingles or coating. If tiles need to be lifted to see the underlayment, we'll tell you why before we do it.

sections.h2: Signs your roof needs a repair
sections.body: Some problems show up inside the house first; others are easy to spot from the yard. Call us if you notice any of these:
bullets: Water stains, bubbling paint or sagging drywall on a ceiling
Broken, slipped or missing tiles visible from the ground
Shingles that are lifted, creased or missing after wind
Granules from shingles collecting at downspouts
Blisters, cracks or bare spots on a foam or flat roof
Water standing on a flat roof two days after rain
Gaps or dried-out sealant around vents, skylights and walls

sections.h2: A simple maintenance calendar for Arizona
sections.body: A roof needs less attention than most parts of a house, but timing helps. This schedule fits most Valley homes:
bullets: Spring: inspection and any repairs before monsoon season begins June 15
During monsoon (June 15–September 30): check from the ground after big storms for displaced tiles or debris
Fall: clear valleys, gutters and roof drains of leaves and storm debris
Every few years: recoat foam and coated flat roofs as the coating wears
Around 20–25 years on a tile roof: have the underlayment evaluated

sections.h2: Repair now or plan a replacement?
sections.body:
A repair is the right call when the problem is isolated and the rest of the roof is sound. If we find widespread brittle underlayment, shingles worn bare across several slopes, or a foam roof worn through to the foam, we'll tell you honestly that repeated patching won't hold.

Either way, you'll get photos and a clear estimate. If replacement makes more sense, see our roof replacement page, and for pricing factors, the roofing cost guide.

faqs: How do I know if my roof is leaking?

Look for water stains on ceilings or walls, peeling paint near the ceiling line, damp insulation in the attic, daylight through roof boards, or a musty smell. Outside, look for broken or slipped tiles, missing shingles, or bubbling on a foam roof.
Can you repair a tile roof without replacing it?

Usually, yes. Broken tiles can be replaced individually, and isolated underlayment problems can be repaired by lifting the tiles in that area. If the underlayment is failing across the whole roof, an underlayment replacement (tile re-felt) may be the better long-term fix.
What causes most roof leaks in Arizona?

Aged underlayment beneath tile, cracked or displaced tiles, worn flashing at walls and penetrations, clogged valleys and drains, and weathered coatings on flat and foam roofs. Monsoon winds and heavy rain expose these weak spots.
How often should I have roof maintenance done?
For most homes, once a year plus after major storms. Foam and coated flat roofs also need recoating on a schedule, typically every several years depending on the coating thickness and exposure.
Is it worth repairing an old roof?

If the problem is isolated and the rest of the roof is in good shape, a repair is usually the smart choice. If you are repairing the same roof again and again, replacement can cost less over time. We'll give you an honest recommendation.
What should I do if my roof is leaking right now?

Move furniture and valuables away from the leak, put a bucket under drips, and if the ceiling is bulging with water, carefully poke a small hole to let it drain into a bucket. Then call us at 602-548-3770, Monday to Friday, 7 am to 5 pm. If we don't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours.
Do you repair roofs you didn't install?
Yes. We repair roofs regardless of who installed them. We'll match the existing materials as closely as possible and tell you if we see other issues while we're up there.
How long does a typical roof repair take?

Many repairs, like replacing a few tiles or resealing a vent, take a few hours. Larger jobs, such as repairing underlayment in one section of a tile roof, can take a day or more. We'll give you a time frame with the estimate.
How much does a roof repair cost?

It depends on the roof type, how much area is affected, access and what's causing the problem. Our roofing cost guide at /resources/roofing-cost-guide/ covers the main factors, and every roof is different, so we'll give you an estimate after we see it.
Why does my roof only leak during monsoon storms?

Monsoon rain often comes sideways with strong wind, which pushes water under tiles and past flashing that stays dry in a gentle rain. A leak that only appears in those storms usually points to a flashing, valley or underlayment weak spot.
Can I replace a broken roof tile myself?
We don't recommend it. Walking on tile can crack more tiles, and a slipped tile or loose nail can leave a gap in the underlayment. A roofer can replace the tile and check the area beneath it.
Can you match my existing tiles or shingles?

We match materials as closely as possible. Older tile profiles and shingle colors are sometimes discontinued, and new pieces can look slightly different until they weather. We'll show you options before we start.
Can you set up yearly maintenance for my roof?
Yes. Call the office at 602-548-3770 and we'll schedule a yearly check, ideally in spring before monsoon season. If we don't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours.

roof-replacement-services.title: Roof Replacement & Re-Roofing, Gilbert AZ | Integrity Roofing
roof-replacement-services.desc: Tile, shingle, foam and flat roof replacement and re-roofing in Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler, Phoenix & the East Valley. Family-owned since 1993. Call 602-548-3770.
roof-replacement-services.h1: Roof replacement built for the Arizona sun
roof-replacement-services.lead: When repairs no longer make sense, we replace your roof with the right system for your home or building, from tile underlayment replacement to a full tear-off and new roof.
roof-replacement-services.answer: You likely need a roof replacement if your roof is near the end of its expected life, leaks in several places, has widespread cracked tiles or granule loss, or the underlayment beneath tile has become brittle. In Arizona, tile roofs are often "re-felted": the tiles are lifted, new underlayment is installed, and the tiles are reinstalled.
roof-replacement-services.card_text: Re-roofs, tile underlayment replacement and new roofs.

sections.body:
"Re-roofing" can mean different things. On a tile roof, it often means removing the tiles, replacing the worn underlayment, and reinstalling the existing tiles (replacing any broken ones). On shingle roofs, it typically means a complete tear-off down to the deck and new shingles. A full replacement may also include new decking, flashing and ventilation.

We'll explain which option fits your roof, what's included, and why.

sections.h2: Signs it's time to replace your roof
sections.body: Age alone doesn't decide it, but these signs mean it's time for a serious look:
bullets: Leaks in more than one area, or the same leak returning
Brittle, torn or exposed underlayment beneath tile
Curling, cracked or bald shingles and heavy granule loss
Sagging roof lines or soft spots in the deck
Foam roof worn through the coating to bare foam
The roof is near or past its expected lifespan

sections.body: The exact scope depends on your roof, and your estimate spells it out. A typical re-roof covers:
bullets: Removing the old roofing down to the deck, or lifting and stacking tiles on a re-felt
Inspecting the deck and replacing damaged or soft boards (noted on the estimate as a possible extra)
New underlayment across the roof
New flashing at walls, valleys and penetrations where needed
Reinstalling tile, or installing new shingles, foam or flat roofing
Replacing broken tiles with matching or close-matching tiles
Clean-up of the site and a final walkthrough

sections.body:
Many Valley neighborhoods have HOA rules on roof material, profile and color. If you're keeping your existing tile on a re-felt, approval may be simple, but if you're changing the look of the roof, most HOAs want to review it first. Check your HOA's process early, since reviews can take time.

Most Valley cities also require a permit for re-roofing. Requirements vary by city, and we'll let you know what applies to your property.

sections.h2: How to read a roofing estimate
sections.body: When you compare estimates, make sure they describe the same job. Look for:
bullets: The roof areas included, including patios and flat sections
Whether it's a tear-off, a re-felt, or new roofing over the existing deck
The underlayment, roofing material and flashing to be used
How damaged decking is handled and priced
Clean-up and disposal of old materials
Payment terms and financing options

sections.body:
A few simple steps make the work go smoothly. Move vehicles out of the garage and driveway so materials can be delivered and crews can work safely. Take down wall hangings on walls that share a roof line, since vibration can shake them loose, and cover items stored in the attic or garage, where dust can fall.

Keep pets inside or away from the work area, and let neighbors know work is coming. Expect noise during the workday. Most homeowners stay home during a re-roof.

sections.h2: Timing a re-roof around Arizona weather
sections.body:
Spring and fall are popular for re-roofs because the weather is mild and dry. Work continues through summer, with crews starting early in the day to avoid the worst heat. During monsoon season, June 15–September 30, we watch forecasts closely so the roof isn't left open when a storm is likely.

If your tile roof is past the 20–25 year mark and has started to leak, scheduling before monsoon season gives you the best protection.

faqs: How long does a roof replacement take?
Most residential roof replacements take a few days once work begins, depending on size, roof type, weather and whether decking needs repair. We'll give you a timeline with your estimate.
What is a tile re-felt or underlayment replacement?

On a tile roof, the tiles themselves can last 50 years or more, but the underlayment beneath them wears out sooner. A re-felt removes the tiles, installs new underlayment, and reinstalls the tiles, replacing any that are broken.
Can a new roof be installed over my old one?
Sometimes on shingle roofs, but we generally recommend a full tear-off so the deck can be inspected and the new roof works as designed. Tile roofs should not be layered.
Do I need a permit to replace my roof?
Most Valley cities require a permit for re-roofing. Requirements vary by city, and we'll let you know what applies to your property.
Will I need to leave my home during the replacement?
Usually not. It will be noisy during the workday, and we recommend moving cars out of the driveway and keeping pets inside or away from the work area.
How much does a roof replacement cost?

It depends on roof size, pitch, material, the condition of the deck and how many layers need removal. Our roofing cost guide at /resources/roofing-cost-guide/ explains the main factors, and every roof is different, so we'll give you a clear estimate after inspecting yours. Financing options are available.
Which roof type is best for Arizona?

Tile and foam roofs hold up very well in Arizona heat; shingles are a cost-effective choice for many homes. The best choice depends on your home's design, your HOA and your budget. See our roof types page for a comparison.
What happens if the crew finds damaged decking?

Decking can only be fully checked once the old roofing is off. If we find soft or rotted boards, we'll show you and replace them so the new roof has a solid base. Your estimate explains how decking repairs are handled.
Do I need HOA approval to replace my roof?
Often, yes, especially if you're changing the roof's material or color. Check your HOA's guidelines and approval process before work is scheduled.
Can my existing tiles be reused?

Usually. Concrete and clay tiles often last decades longer than the underlayment beneath them. On a re-felt, we lift the tiles, install new underlayment, and reinstall the tiles, replacing any that are cracked or broken.
What's the best time of year to replace a roof in Arizona?
Spring and fall offer the mildest weather, but roofs are replaced year-round. If your roof is already leaking, it's best to get it done before monsoon season starts June 15.
Is financing available for a roof replacement?
Yes, financing options are available. Ask about them during your estimate.

roof-inspections.title: Roof Inspections in Gilbert & Phoenix, AZ | Integrity Roofing
roof-inspections.desc: Thorough roof inspections for homeowners, buyers, sellers and property managers in Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler & Phoenix. Find hidden damage before monsoon season.
roof-inspections.h1: Roof inspections that catch problems early
roof-inspections.lead: A roof can look fine from the street and still have cracked tiles, failing underlayment or worn flashing. An inspection tells you exactly where your roof stands and what, if anything, needs attention.
roof-inspections.answer: A roof inspection is a hands-on check of your roof covering, underlayment (where visible), flashing, penetrations, valleys, drainage and signs of leaks. In Arizona, it's smart to inspect your roof once a year, ideally in spring before monsoon season, plus after major storms and before buying or selling a home.
roof-inspections.card_text: Find hidden damage before it becomes a leak.

sections.h2: Why inspect a roof that "looks fine"
sections.body:
Most roof damage isn't visible from the ground. Tiles crack from foot traffic and heat, underlayment dries out under the tiles, and sealants around vents shrink in the sun. By the time there's a stain on the ceiling, the water has usually been getting in for a while.

A routine inspection is the least expensive way to protect the most expensive part of your home's exterior.
Some timing makes more sense than others. Book a roof inspection:
bullets: In spring, before monsoon season starts June 15
After a monsoon storm with strong wind, heavy rain or falling branches
Before you buy a home, so you know the roof's condition before closing
Before you list a home, so there are no surprises during the buyer's inspection
When a tile roof reaches about 20–25 years, when underlayment often starts to wear
Before adding solar panels or other equipment to the roof
When you notice a stain, a drip or broken tiles

sections.h2: What to expect on inspection day
sections.body:
We'll ask about any leaks or stains you've seen, then inspect the roof itself, working carefully so we don't crack tiles while we walk. We check the covering, flashing, valleys, penetrations and drainage, and photograph anything that needs attention.

When we're done, we walk you through the photos and explain what we found in plain language. If repairs are needed, you'll get a clear estimate. If the roof is in good shape, we'll tell you that too.

A general home inspector covers the whole house and often views the roof from a ladder or the ground. A roofing contractor looks more closely at the roof alone: how the underlayment is holding up, whether flashing is sound, and roughly how much life is left.

For buyers, that helps you plan for repairs or negotiate before closing. For sellers, an inspection before listing lets you fix small issues on your own schedule instead of during escrow.

sections.h2: What you can check from the ground
sections.body: Between inspections, a quick look from the yard can catch problems early. Never climb onto the roof to check. Look for:
bullets: Cracked, slipped or missing tiles, especially along ridges and edges
Lifted or missing shingles after wind
Debris piled in valleys or around roof drains
Peeling or bare patches on foam or coated flat roofs
New stains on ceilings or around light fixtures inside

features: Cracked, broken, slipped or missing tiles and shingles; foam and coating wear.
Signs of water entry, staining, and soft or damaged decking.
Walls, chimneys, skylights, valleys and roof-to-wall transitions.
Plumbing vents, HVAC, solar mounts and satellite dishes.
Brittle underlayment, dried sealants and coating breakdown.
Photos of what we found and our recommendation: repair, maintain, or replace.

faqs: How often should a roof be inspected in Arizona?
At least once a year, ideally in spring before monsoon season begins June 15, and again after any major storm. Older roofs benefit from more frequent checks.
Should I get a roof inspection when buying a home?

Yes. A general home inspector looks at the roof, but a roofing contractor can give you a closer look at the roof's condition, the remaining life, and what repairs may be needed — useful information before you close.
What happens during a roof inspection?
We check the roof covering, flashing, valleys, penetrations, drainage and visible signs of leaks, document what we find with photos, and explain our recommendation.
How long does a roof inspection take?
Most residential inspections take about an hour, depending on the roof's size, pitch and access.
Do I need to be home for the inspection?
It helps if you can be there so we can walk you through what we found, but it isn't always required for an exterior roof inspection. We'll arrange the details when we schedule.
Can an inspection help with an insurance claim?
Our photos and findings document the roof's condition and any damage, which you can share with your insurance company. Coverage decisions are made by your insurer.
How much does a roof inspection cost?

It depends on the roof's size, type and access. Call the office at 602-548-3770 and we'll explain what to expect. For repair and replacement pricing factors, see our roofing cost guide at /resources/roofing-cost-guide/.
Can you tell how much life my roof has left?
We can give you a general idea based on the roof type, age and condition. On tile roofs, the underlayment usually decides the remaining life, and it often starts wearing out after about 20–25 years.
Do you inspect foam and flat roofs?
Yes. On foam and flat roofs we look at the coating, blisters, punctures, seams, ponding water and the drains and scuppers that carry water off the roof.
Will walking on my tile roof break tiles?
Tile can crack if it's stepped on in the wrong place. Experienced roofers walk where tiles are supported and avoid the weak points. That's also why we recommend homeowners stay off tile roofs.
What should I tell you before the inspection?
Let us know about any leaks or stains, when they appear, the roof's approximate age, and any past repairs. That helps us focus on the areas that matter most.
What happens if the inspection finds a problem?
We'll show you photos, explain whether it's a repair, maintenance or replacement issue, and give you a clear estimate. There's no pressure to decide on the spot.

damaged-roof.title: Storm & Damaged Roof Repair, Gilbert AZ | Integrity Roofing
damaged-roof.desc: Monsoon, wind and storm-damaged roof repair in Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler & Phoenix. Inspection, photos and lasting repairs from a family-owned roofer.
damaged-roof.h1: Damaged roof? Let's find out how bad it is
damaged-roof.lead: Monsoon winds, falling branches, hail and heat can all damage a roof. We inspect it, document the damage, and make a repair that holds up to the next storm.
damaged-roof.answer: After a storm, look for missing or lifted shingles, cracked or displaced tiles, punctures or exposed foam on flat roofs, debris in valleys, and new stains on ceilings. If you see damage, call Integrity Roofing during business hours to inspect and document it. Don't walk on a damaged roof yourself.
damaged-roof.card_text: Monsoon, wind and storm damage repair.

sections.h2: Common types of roof damage in Arizona
sections.body: Arizona's monsoon season (June 15–September 30) brings sudden high winds and heavy rain. Combined with year-round heat and UV, that's a tough environment for any roof.
bullets: Wind-lifted or missing shingles
Cracked, broken or slipped tiles
Punctures, blisters or exposed foam on flat roofs
Damage from falling branches or debris
Water intrusion from clogged valleys and drains
Heat-cracked sealants and flashing

sections.h2: What to do after a storm
sections.body:
1. Stay safe. Don't climb onto a wet or damaged roof.
  2. Protect the inside. Move belongings away from leaks and contain dripping water.
  3. Take photos. Photograph visible damage from the ground and any interior water stains.
  4. Call us. Phone 602-548-3770 (Monday to Friday, 7 am to 5 pm) to schedule an inspection. If we don't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours.
  5. Contact your insurer if you plan to file a claim. Our photos and findings can help document the damage.

sections.h2: Damage you can't see from the ground
sections.body:
Some storm damage is obvious, like a tile lying in the yard. Much of it isn't. Wind can lift tiles just enough to crack them or shift them off their battens without them falling. It can break the seal on shingles so they flap in the next storm, or drive rain under flashing and into the underlayment.

Signs often show up days or weeks later: a stain that slowly spreads, a musty smell in a closet, or a drip during the next storm. If a strong storm passed over your home, an inspection is worth it even if nothing looks wrong.

We look at the whole roof, not just the obvious spot. That includes the slopes facing the wind, ridges and edges where tiles and shingles lift first, valleys where debris piles up, flashing at walls and penetrations, and drains and scuppers on flat sections.

We photograph the damage and explain what's storm-related, what's normal wear, and what we recommend. That distinction matters if you're talking with your insurance company.

Not all roof damage comes from storms. Months of high heat and UV dry out sealants, crack the coating on foam roofs, and make older underlayment brittle. Then the first monsoon storm finds the weak spots.

If your roof leaked in a storm that didn't seem severe, heat-related wear may be part of the cause. A spring inspection catches most of these issues before the storms arrive.

Many homeowner policies cover sudden storm damage but not gradual wear. Your insurer decides what's covered. What we can do is document the roof's condition with photos and a clear explanation of what we found, which you can share with your insurance company.

Report damage to your insurer promptly, keep your own photos, and hold onto receipts for anything you spend protecting your home.

faqs: How can I tell if my roof was damaged in a storm?

From the ground, look for missing or lifted shingles, broken or shifted tiles, debris on the roof, dents in gutters, and granules collecting at downspouts. Inside, check ceilings and the attic for new stains or damp spots.
Should I get on the roof to check for damage?
No. Wet and damaged roofs are slippery, and walking on tile can break more tiles. Let a roofer inspect it.
Will insurance cover storm damage to my roof?

Many homeowner policies cover sudden storm damage, but not wear and tear. Coverage depends on your policy and your insurer's decision. We can document the damage with photos for you to share with your insurance company.
What if my roof is damaged on an evening or weekend?

Our office is open Monday to Friday, 7 am to 5 pm, and closed on Saturday and Sunday. Call 602-548-3770; if we don't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours. In the meantime, protect belongings inside and photograph the damage.
Can a damaged roof be repaired, or does it need to be replaced?
Most storm damage is repairable. Replacement is usually recommended only when damage is widespread or the roof was already near the end of its life.
How can I prepare my roof for monsoon season?

Have it inspected in spring, before monsoon season starts June 15. Replace broken tiles or shingles, clear valleys, gutters and roof drains, trim overhanging branches, and reseal flashing and penetrations.
How soon after a storm should my roof be inspected?
As soon as you can schedule it, especially if you see damage or a new stain. Damage left alone can let water reach the deck and the inside of your home, and the next monsoon storm can make it worse.
Can monsoon wind damage a tile roof?
Yes. Strong gusts can lift, crack or shift tiles, especially along ridges, hips and edges. Wind-driven rain can also get under displaced tiles and reach the underlayment.
Why did a stain appear days after the storm?
Water can soak into underlayment, decking or insulation and travel before it shows up on a ceiling. A stain that appears later still points to a roof problem worth checking.
Should I put a tarp on my roof?
We don't recommend climbing onto a damaged roof yourself. A tarp can limit water for a short time, but it isn't a repair, and installing one safely takes care. Call us to schedule an inspection.
How much does storm damage repair cost?

It depends on the type and extent of the damage and the roof material. See our roofing cost guide at /resources/roofing-cost-guide/ for the main factors. Every roof is different, so we'll give you an estimate after inspecting yours.
Can debris on the roof cause leaks?
Yes. Leaves and branches collect in valleys and around drains, slow the water down and push it sideways under tiles or onto seams. Clearing debris after storms is simple, effective maintenance.

sections.body: For property managers, unplanned leaks mean tenant complaints and damaged inventory. Regular inspections and scheduled recoating spread costs out, extend the roof's life, and help you plan capital expenses instead of reacting to emergencies.

sections.h2: Drainage is where most flat roofs fail
sections.body:
Flat roofs aren't perfectly flat; they rely on slight slope, drains and scuppers to move water off. When debris clogs a drain or the roof settles, water sits. Standing water two days after rain, often called ponding, wears coatings faster, adds weight and finds its way into seams.

Keeping drains and scuppers clear, especially before and during monsoon season (June 15–September 30), is one of the simplest ways to protect a commercial roof. Where ponding keeps returning, we'll talk with you about options to improve drainage.

Many commercial roofs can be extended rather than replaced. If the roof is structurally sound and mostly dry, a foam recoat or an elastomeric coating can renew the surface and reflect sunlight. If water has soaked large areas of the roof, or the system is past repair, replacement is the better investment.

We inspect the roof, check for wet areas and wear, and explain which path makes sense. For pricing factors, see our roofing cost guide. Every roof is different, so your estimate is based on your building.

Commercial work affects more people than a home project. We'll coordinate the schedule with you, confirm how we'll reach the roof (exterior ladder, roof hatch or interior access), and plan where materials and equipment will go so entrances and parking stay usable.

It helps to let tenants know when work is scheduled, especially for jobs that involve noise or odor from coatings near HVAC intakes. Clear communication up front prevents most complaints.

faqs: What types of commercial roofs do you work on?
Spray polyurethane foam, elastomeric-coated roofs, flat and low-slope systems such as modified bitumen, and tile or shingle on sloped commercial buildings.
How often should a commercial roof be inspected?
At least twice a year — typically spring and fall — and after major storms. Regular inspections catch drainage and flashing issues early.
Can a commercial roof be recoated instead of replaced?

Often, yes. If the existing roof is structurally sound and mostly dry, a coating or foam recoat can extend its life for less than a full replacement. An inspection will tell us if your roof is a good candidate.
Do you work with property managers and HOAs?
Yes. We work with property managers, HOAs and building owners on multi-family and commercial properties.
Can you work around our business hours?
We'll coordinate scheduling with you to minimize disruption to your tenants, customers and operations.
Why are reflective roofs popular on Arizona commercial buildings?
Light-colored, reflective coatings reflect sunlight and reduce heat absorbed by the roof, which can help lower cooling demand in hot climates.
What is ponding water, and why does it matter?
Ponding is water that stays on a flat roof two days or more after rain. It wears coatings faster, adds weight and can work into seams and flashing, so it's worth fixing the drainage issue behind it.
How often does a foam roof need recoating?
Typically every several years, depending on the coating type, its thickness and how much sun the roof gets. Regular inspections show when the coating is getting thin.
Do HVAC units cause roof leaks?
They can. Flashing around curbs and penetrations wears out, and service technicians walking to the units can damage the roof surface. These areas get extra attention during inspections.
What's the difference between foam roofing and an elastomeric coating?

Spray foam is a roof system that adds insulation and is protected by a coating. An elastomeric coating is a flexible, reflective layer applied over an existing roof surface. Our foam roofing and elastomeric coating pages explain each in more detail.
How much does commercial roofing cost?

It depends on the roof size, system, condition, access and scope. See our roofing cost guide at /resources/roofing-cost-guide/ for the main factors. Every roof is different, so we'll give you an estimate after inspecting your building.
Do you need access through the building to reach the roof?
Sometimes. Some buildings have an exterior ladder; others are reached through an interior roof hatch. We'll confirm access with you before the visit.
